territory: Signed-out surface: auth-page client components (login, signup+trivia, forgot/reset password, verify-email), the signup server action chain they drive, onboarding (/welcome wizard + legacy /onboarding), and the landing page (src/app/page.tsx + src/components/landing/**)

findings.title: Email case is never normalized at signup/login while password reset lowercases: any account registered with an uppercase letter in its email can NEVER receive a reset link (silent, permanent lockout), and one mailbox can register twice
findings.expected: One mailbox = one account, findable by any casing: signup, login and reset should agree on a canonical (lowercased) form of the address, per taxonomy 6e.
findings.actual: Signup stores the address exactly as typed; login looks it up exactly as typed; but the forgot-password flow lowercases before lookup. A member who signed up as 'Amy@Gmail.com' gets 'check your inbox' from the reset form and no mail ever arrives, forever, with no signal anywhere (the identical-answer anti-oracle design hides the miss). Two rows for one mailbox ('Amy@x.com' + 'amy@x.com') are also possible since the unique index is case-sensitive.
findings.evidence: registerUser stores raw case: `email: parsed.data.email` (actions.ts:149) — signupSchema uses `z.email(...)` (validators.ts:18) which validates format but applies no lowercase transform, and prisma/schema.prisma:13 is `email String @unique` (Postgres btree, case-sensitive). authorize() looks up raw: `const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } })` (auth.ts:102) — note it builds `const acctKey = email.trim().toLowerCase()` (auth.ts:62) for rate-limit keys and the human-pass, but NOT for the DB lookup. requestPasswordReset destroys the case first: `const raw = ((formData.get("email") as string) ?? "").trim().toLowerCase();` then `prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email: raw } })` (email-actions.ts:160,165) and on a miss returns the identical `{ ok: true }` (by design, line 174), so the mixed-case member sees the 'A reset link is on its way to …' screen (forgot-client.tsx:194) and nothing is ever enqueued. The doomed loop the login comment warns about (login-client.tsx:386-390 'telling someone their password is wrong when it isn't sends them into a doomed reset loop') is exactly what ships for these accounts: wrong-case login says 'Invalid email or password', and the reset path is a black hole. signHumanPass already lowercases (human-pass-rule.ts:16 `email.toLowerCase()`), so the codebase is internally split on the convention.
findings.fixDirection: Pick lowercase as canonical: (1) lowercase in signupSchema (z.email().transform or .toLowerCase() in registerUser before findUnique/create); (2) lowercase in authorize() before the findUnique (use acctKey, which already exists); (3) run a one-time idempotent SQL migration lowercasing existing User.email rows (guard: check for case-only duplicate pairs first and resolve manually — count today is likely zero); (4) optionally add a functional unique index on lower(email) via migrations-manual to make the invariant structural. Keep requestPasswordReset as-is once the store is canonical.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only proof against prod data: `SELECT email FROM "User" WHERE email <> lower(email);` — any row returned is a member already locked out of reset. Behavioral proof on a test account: sign up via the UI with 'RvAuditTest@example.com', then submit forgot-password for 'rvaudittest@example.com' (lowercased is what the server does anyway) and observe OutboundEmail: no reset row is created.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on a shared normalizeEmail() used by all three flows; plus a security-regressions-style test asserting registerUser and authorize both lowercase before hitting the User table.

findings.title: proxy.ts sends signed-out visitors to /login?callbackUrl=<path>, but the login page only reads ?next= — every deep link (shared post, letter, profile, notification email) is lost and the member lands on /feed after signing in
findings.expected: A signed-out person clicking a shared link to /letters/xyz signs in and lands on /letters/xyz.
findings.actual: They land on /feed, always. The parameter the proxy writes is never read by anything.
findings.evidence: proxy.ts:242-245: `const loginUrl = new URL("/login", request.url); loginUrl.searchParams.set("callbackUrl", pathname); return NextResponse.redirect(loginUrl);`. The login success path (login-client.tsx:403) is `window.location.href = nextPathFromLocation();`, and nextPathFromLocation reads only `next`: `safeNextPath(new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("next"), fallback)` (next-path.ts:35). A repo-wide grep for callbackUrl finds only the proxy write and two `signOut({ callbackUrl: "/" })` calls (sidebar.tsx:481, letterhead-profile.tsx:1314) — no reader. The only producer of `?next=` is the catchups join page (src/app/catchups/join/[token]/page.tsx:145,150), so that one flow works and every proxy-initiated bounce silently drops the destination. This is distinct from tracked bug 5b (signed-out unknown routes bounce to login instead of 404) — this is about KNOWN routes losing their destination.
findings.fixDirection: Change proxy.ts to set `next` instead of `callbackUrl` (value = pathname + search, so query strings survive too), since safeNextPath already validates it against open-redirects. Alternatively teach nextPathFromLocation to fall back to callbackUrl; the single-param option is cleaner. Mirror on the signup path if desired (signup already forwards next through /welcome).
findings.reproPlan: Signed out, open http://localhost:3000/directory — observe redirect to /login?callbackUrl=%2Fdirectory. Sign in with the dev login; observe landing on /feed, not /directory.
findings.gateOrTest: Playwright spec: visit a gated route signed out, sign in through the form, expect.poll final URL to equal the original route.

findings.title: Avatar upload (onboarding photo step + settings) promises 15MB but ships the raw file through a server action, which Vercel hard-caps at ~4.5MB — typical phone photos fail, and the photo step's missing try/catch turns that failure into a permanently stuck spinner
findings.expected: Any image the UI accepts ('Photo must be under 15MB') uploads successfully, or fails with an actionable message.
findings.actual: On Vercel, a 5-15MB photo is rejected by the platform (413 FUNCTION_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE) before the action runs. photo-step.tsx line 49 `const result = await updateAvatar(fd);` has no try/catch, so the rejected fetch throws, `busy` stays true forever (button disabled, spinner spinning), and no toast appears. Modern phone photos are routinely 4-12MB, so this hits a large fraction of members on the onboarding step itself.
findings.evidence: Client gate: `if (file.size > 15 * 1024 * 1024) { toast.error("Photo must be under 15MB") }` (photo-step.tsx:42-44) then `fd.set("file", file); const result = await updateAvatar(fd);` — bytes through the action. Server gate agrees: `const MAX_AVATAR_INPUT = 15 * 1024 * 1024;` (settings/actions.ts:20) and `if (file.size > MAX_AVATAR_INPUT) return { error: "Photo must be under 15MB" }` (line 215). The repo itself documents the platform cap: upload-client.ts:14-16 — 'The caller then falls back to its classic server-proxied upload, which is capped at ~4.5MB on Vercel'. next.config.ts `serverActions: { bodySizeLimit: "25mb" }` lifts only Next's own limit (and proxyClientMaxBodySize only matters self-hosted); Vercel's serverless request-body ceiling is a platform constant the config cannot raise. Avatars have NO presigned direct-to-R2 path — directUploadPut supports only `kind: "post" | "collection"` (upload-client.ts:19-21). The same platform cap likely also bites the Collection contribute server action (contributePhoto — the config comment at next.config.ts:106-110 expects 20MB photos through it), flagged here for the collection-territory investigator.
findings.fixDirection: Route avatars through the existing presign path (add kind "avatar" to /api/upload/presign + directUploadPut, then pass the staged key to updateAvatar for the sharp/512px pass server-side reading from R2), or downscale client-side before posting (src/lib/image-downscale.ts exists) so the wire size stays under ~4MB. Independently, wrap the photo-step await in try/catch/finally so busy always resets and a real message shows.
findings.reproPlan: Against the production deployment with a test account: attempt an avatar upload with a 6MB JPEG on the /welcome photo step; observe the network tab 413 and the spinner never resolving. (Local dev will NOT reproduce — no platform cap — which is why it survived QA.)
findings.gateOrTest: E2e spec uploading a >4.5MB fixture through the avatar path once the fix lands; unit-level assertion that every FormData file path either presigns or client-downscales below 4MB.

findings.title: Nine auth/onboarding client call sites await server actions with no try/catch: any transient failure (network blip, deploy mid-session, cold-start timeout, 413) leaves the button permanently disabled in its busy label with no error shown
findings.expected: Every awaited server action mirrors login-client.tsx:364-409 and signup-form.tsx:391-444, which wrap in try/catch/finally so the pending flag always resets and the member gets 'Something went wrong. Please try again.'
findings.actual: A rejected action promise escapes the handler: the busy state set before the await never resets (button stuck on 'Sending...'/'Saving...'), and the rejection is unhandled. Chaos cases from the brief (DB slow/down mid-request, session/deployment skew) all land here.
findings.evidence: forgot-client.tsx:67+82: `setSending(true); ... const result = await requestPasswordReset(formData);` — no try, no finally; a throw exits with sending=true (button disabled at line 156 `disabled={sending}`, label 'Sending...'). reset-client.tsx:116-117: `setBusy(true); const result = await resetPassword({ token, password });` same shape ('Saving...' forever, the typed password stranded); and after success, line 135 `const signedIn = await signIn(...)` — a throw there strands the member on the 'we are signing you in now' screen with the redirect setTimeout never scheduled (password IS changed, so at least manual login works). verify-client.tsx:103-105: `setBusy(true); ... const result = await resendVerification();`. trivia-gate.tsx:45: `getTriviaQuestion().then(setQuestion)` with no .catch — a rejection leaves the question '...' and the Check button disabled forever (line 202 `disabled={!question ...}`), and swapQuestion (line 60) has the same hole. register-step.tsx:81-83, houses-step.tsx:66-72 (`handleSave`) and its mount effect (line 56, `await getOnboardingHouses()` — loading stuck true), photo-step (covered in the 4.5MB finding), and legacy onboarding/page.tsx:26 (`await updateProfile(formData)` then router.push with no error branch at all).
findings.fixDirection: Mechanical: wrap each await in try/catch with the shared generic sentence and move the busy-reset into finally, exactly as login-client/signup-form already do. For trivia-gate's fetch, add .catch that sets an inline error with a retry button (a failed question fetch currently has no recovery but reload).
findings.reproPlan: Local: load /forgot-password, stop the dev server, submit — button sticks on 'Sending...' with a console unhandled-rejection; same probe per site.
findings.gateOrTest: ESLint discipline or a small unit test greping auth/onboarding clients for awaited actions outside try (same pattern as security-regressions.test.mjs); or per-form Playwright specs with route interception returning 500.

findings.title: Turnstile widget's `dead` latch is permanent: one challenge error-callback bricks every subsequent sign-in/signup/reset submit in that tab (server fails closed on the missing token), and only a full page reload recovers
findings.expected: The widget's own header comment promises 'a broken third party never bricks sign-in' — after a transient challenge error, a later submit should re-attempt the challenge (Turnstile supports reset()) rather than permanently give up.
findings.actual: After `error-callback` fires once (transient network loss while the challenge brews, an extension interfering, a Cloudflare hiccup after retries are exhausted), `dead.current = true` forever. Every later getToken() resolves null instantly, the form submits tokenless, and the server refuses: verifyTurnstile has `if (!token) return false;` when a secret is configured, so authorize() throws BotCheckFailed and the member sees the bot-check message on every attempt with correct credentials, with no hint that reloading fixes it. The fail-open posture only covers the SERVER side (siteverify unreachable / key unset); the client-side failure modes (script blocked, challenge error, 12s timeout) all fail closed.
findings.evidence: turnstile-widget.tsx:107-110: `"error-callback": () => { dead.current = true; waiters.current.splice(0).forEach((w) => w(null)); }` — no `window.turnstile.reset(...)`, no un-latching, unlike "expired-callback" (105) which does reset. Line 136: `if (dead.current) return Promise.resolve(null);`. turnstile.ts:86: `if (!token) return false;` (after the secret-configured check), and auth.ts:91-94: `if (!human) { ... throw new BotCheckFailed(); }`. registerUser and requestPasswordReset share the same fate via verifyHumanFromForm (turnstile.ts:130-135).
findings.fixDirection: In error-callback, reset the widget and clear the latch (optionally after a short backoff, and only latch dead after N consecutive errors); alternatively have getToken(), when it finds dead=true, attempt one re-render/reset before resolving null. Also worth an explicit user-facing sentence for the tokenless-refusal case suggesting a reload, since the server cannot distinguish it from a bot.
findings.reproPlan: Local with TURNSTILE_DEV_REAL=1: load /login, use DevTools request blocking on challenges.cloudflare.com AFTER the script loads to force the challenge to error, then unblock and submit repeatedly — every attempt returns bot-check until reload.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on a widget harness: simulate error-callback then assert a later getToken() attempts a reset rather than resolving null.

findings.title: Trivia pass expiry (30-min TTL) or cookies-blocked leaves the signup register step unrecoverable: registerUser demands the entry question but the UI has no way back to the trivia step, so the filled form dead-ends (cookie-blocked browsers loop forever)
findings.expected: If the server refuses because the gate pass is missing/expired, the flow returns the person to the trivia step (keeping their typed form state), or the pass is refreshed transparently.
findings.actual: registerUser returns { error: "Please answer the entry question before signing up." } which renders as a red line under the form; the step state machine only ever moves trivia→register (onPass at signup-client.tsx:392) — there is no setStep("trivia") anywhere after that, so the only recovery is a full reload, which discards every field. A visitor with cookies disabled passes the client-side gate (checkTrivia returns ok regardless of whether the browser stored rv_trivia_pass) and then hits this error on every submit, indefinitely, with an instruction they cannot follow.
findings.evidence: actions.ts:17-21: `if (!(await hasPassedTrivia())) { return { error: "Please answer the entry question before signing up." }; }`. TTL: trivia-actions.ts:83 `const TOKEN_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;` and hasPassedTrivia (226-242) requires BOTH rv_trivia_pass and rv_trivia_id cookies (231: `if (!token || !browserId) return false;`). Note also the id cookie's maxAge is set at FIRST attempt (line 182-190), so someone whose first wrong attempt was 29 minutes before their pass loses the id cookie a minute later and the still-valid pass stops verifying. signup-client.tsx: `const [step, setStep] = useState<Step>("trivia")` (line 30) and the only transition is `onPass={() => setStep("register")}` (392).
findings.fixDirection: Map that specific server error to setStep("trivia") in SignupForm's error branch (lift the trivia error into a callback prop so signup-client can flip back while React state preserves the form fields, since the component stays mounted under AnimatePresence), and refresh the rv_trivia_id maxAge whenever the pass is minted. Optionally detect document.cookie-disabled up front and show a plain 'this site needs cookies to sign up' notice.
findings.reproPlan: Local: pass trivia, delete the rv_trivia_pass cookie in DevTools, submit the filled form — observe the dead-end error with no route back; or block all cookies in a fresh profile and walk the flow.
findings.gateOrTest: Playwright: clear the pass cookie between steps, submit, expect the trivia step to return with the form state intact.

findings.title: joinBatchGroup is find-then-create with no unique constraint on Group.name: two same-batch signups racing (launch day is exactly when this happens) create duplicate 'Batch of {year}' groups and permanently split the batch membership
findings.expected: One group per batch year, however many members register concurrently — per taxonomy 6d, the DB constraint is the only real guard for find-or-create.
findings.actual: Both concurrent registrations findFirst → null → both create → two rows named 'Batch of 2019'; each member lands in a different one, and every later member joins whichever findFirst returns first (nondeterministic order — no orderBy). Catch-ups and batch fan-outs built on the group then address half the batch. No cleanup path exists.
findings.evidence: actions.ts:215-230: `let group = await prisma.group.findFirst({ where: { name }, select: { id: true } }); if (!group) { group = await prisma.group.create({ ... }) }` — the code's own comment concedes 'Group.name is not unique in the schema, so match by exact name'. The membership upsert below it (232-236) is protected by `@@unique` on (groupId,userId), so the pattern was known — it just wasn't applied to the group row itself. Launch is the high-risk window: a WhatsApp-batch-group of classmates signing up within the same minute is the expected adoption pattern, and signup rate limits are per-IP so they do not serialize this.
findings.fixDirection: Add a unique constraint (e.g. a partial/functional unique on name for batch groups, or a dedicated batchYear column with @@unique) via a dated migrations-manual file, switch joinBatchGroup to upsert/`create...catch P2002 then findFirst`, and add a one-time dedupe query merging any existing duplicates' members before the constraint lands.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (provoking it live means racing two real signups against the shared production DB). A read-only check for prior occurrences: `SELECT name, count(*) FROM "Group" WHERE name LIKE 'Batch of %' GROUP BY name HAVING count(*) > 1;`
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test firing two concurrent joinBatchGroup calls against a transaction-wrapped test double; the schema constraint is the real gate.

findings.title: Legacy /onboarding page is orphaned but live, and its updateProfile action writes bio/currentCity/workplace/jobTitle/phone/instagram/linkedin with NO validation — no length caps, no phone normalization — bypassing every rule profileSchema enforces on the same columns
findings.expected: Every write path to a column enforces the same rules (the codebase's own M18 principle, validators.ts:113-120: 'this is the second write path to them, so it gets the same gate').
findings.actual: A signed-in member navigating to /onboarding (it resolves; it is only absent from nav) can submit a multi-hundred-KB bio (server-action bodies accept up to 25MB per next.config), an unnormalized phone, uncapped instagram/linkedin — values profileSchema caps at 1000/24/100/200. Oversized text then flows into every surface that renders these columns (directory cards, profile), the exact over-fetch/rendering weight 6j warns about.
findings.evidence: onboarding/actions.ts:12-20: `const fields = ["bio", "currentCity", "workplace", "jobTitle", "phone", "instagram", "linkedin"]; for (const field of fields) { const value = formData.get(field) as string | null; if (value && value.trim()) { data[field] = value.trim(); } }` then `prisma.user.update({ ... data })` — no Zod, no max, no normalizePhone (compare profileSchema: bio max(1000), phone max(24), instagram max(100), linkedin max(200), validators.ts:56-76). The page is reachable: it sits in (auth)/onboarding, is NOT in proxy publicPaths (so it needs a session — fine), and welcome/page.tsx:13-18 itself calls it 'dead code today ... not linked from anywhere'. Dead-but-routable plus unvalidated write = the gap.
findings.fixDirection: Delete the legacy page and action outright (the /welcome wizard superseded it; welcome/page.tsx's comment says only file-deletion scope stopped it), or if kept, run its input through profileSchema.pick(...) + normalizePhone like settings does. Deletion is the simplification the pre-release audit wants anyway.
findings.reproPlan: Signed in as a test account locally, visit /onboarding, paste a 100KB string into Bio, save; read the row length back via prisma studio (read-only confirm).
findings.gateOrTest: security-regressions.test.mjs-style assertion that (auth)/onboarding/actions.ts no longer exists, or a unit test that its action rejects >1000-char bio.

findings.title: The landing page (and every route) is dynamically rendered because the root layout awaits cookies() for the theme — the 'landing stays statically rendered' claim in proxy.ts is false in shipped code
findings.expected: The signed-in '/'→/feed redirect was deliberately placed in the proxy 'so the landing page stays statically rendered for logged-out visitors' (proxy.ts comment) — i.e. '/' served from CDN with static TTFB, the stated reason auth() was kept out of page.tsx.
findings.actual: RootLayout awaits getThemeCookie() → cookies(), a dynamic API, which opts every route under it — including '/', /login, /signup — into per-request SSR (no ppr/cacheComponents in next.config to give a static shell). The architectural care taken in page.tsx and proxy.ts is silently void: every anonymous landing hit pays a function invocation and cold-start latency, and at 2,000 members' worth of shared-link traffic that is the TTFB profile of the front door.
findings.evidence: layout.tsx:69 (in RootLayout, an async server component): `const theme = (await getThemeCookie()) ?? "light";`; theme.ts:23-25: `export async function getThemeCookie() { const value = (await cookies()).get(THEME_COOKIE)?.value; ... }`. proxy.ts:150-154: 'Handled here rather than in `app/page.tsx` so the landing page stays statically rendered for logged-out visitors: calling `auth()` in the page would opt the whole route into dynamic rendering for everyone.' — cookies() has identical dynamic-rendering semantics to auth(). next.config.ts experimental block contains only optimizePackageImports/serverActions/proxyClientMaxBodySize — no PPR.
findings.fixDirection: Signed-out pages are always light-theme (dark is only entered via settings), so move the theme-cookie read out of the root layout into the (main) layout (or a client-side <ThemeScript> reading document.cookie before paint), letting '/', /login, /signup and the policy pages go static. Verify with `next build` output: '/' should list as prerendered.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only: run a curl against production '/' twice and compare x-vercel-cache headers (MISS/expected dynamic today), or inspect the deployed build output page in the Vercel dashboard — orchestrator-level check.
findings.gateOrTest: A build-output assertion in CI that '/' is static (grep the build manifest), so a future layout edit cannot silently re-dynamify the front door.

findings.title: Signup Join button re-enables during the 1400ms celebration window: a double-click after success fires registerUser again, painting 'An account with this email already exists' over the welcome toast before navigating anyway
findings.expected: After a successful registration the form stays inert for the celebration beat; the one unrepeatable success moment is not interruptible by its own submit button.
findings.actual: `setTimeout(onSuccess, 1400)` schedules navigation, but the `finally { setLoading(false) }` block runs immediately, so `disabled={loading}` (line 680) releases the button for the full 1.4s. A second press re-runs the whole submit: fresh Turnstile getToken, registerUser returns the already-exists error (the P2002/pre-check path), setError paints the red line and hoopoe.react("error") fires mid-celebration; navigation to /welcome still happens at 1400ms, so the member's final frames of signup are a success toast, an error line, and an error-shaking bird at once.
findings.evidence: signup-form.tsx:429-437: `hoopoe.celebrate(3); toast.success("Welcome to the jungle!"); ... setTimeout(onSuccess, 1400);` inside try; lines 442-444: `} finally { setLoading(false); }` — unconditional. Button: line 680 `disabled={loading}`.
findings.fixDirection: Don't reset loading on the success path (leave the button disabled until navigation), e.g. track a `succeeded` flag and make finally `if (!succeeded) setLoading(false)`, or disable on `loading || navigating`.
findings.reproPlan: Local: sign up a throwaway account and double-click Join immediately after the toast appears; observe the error line + error reaction during the celebration.
findings.gateOrTest: Playwright: after submit, assert the button stays disabled until the URL changes to /welcome.

findings.title: signupSchema's year ceilings call new Date().getFullYear() at module load, so a warm serverless instance (or the IST/UTC New Year gap) rejects valid current-year values with 'That year hasn't happened yet'-class errors
findings.expected: Year bounds are evaluated per-validation against the current date (and ideally against IST, where the members are).
findings.actual: `z.number().int().min(1926).max(new Date().getFullYear())` runs the max() computation once when the module is first imported. Two consequences: (a) an instance that stays warm across midnight Dec 31 UTC rejects yearJoined = the new year until it recycles; (b) members in IST enter the new year 5.5 hours before the server does, so on every Jan 1 IST morning the current year is rejected even on a cold instance. Same frozen-at-import pattern on profileSchema (settings) and photoSchema ('That year hasn't happened yet', line 188). The blast radius is small (a few hours a year, +1-year headroom on yearLeft/batchYear absorbs most cases) but yearJoined/taughtFrom/photoYear have no headroom.
findings.evidence: validators.ts:22: `yearJoined: z.number().int().min(1926).max(new Date().getFullYear()).optional(),` — module-scope object literal; zod evaluates the max argument at schema construction, not per parse. Deeper IST instance of tracked note 6's class, which the audit brief explicitly scopes in.
findings.fixDirection: Replace the static max with a refine that computes the ceiling per call (`.refine(v => v <= currentYearIST() + headroom)`), with a small helper that derives 'today' in Asia/Kolkata; one helper shared by all three schemas.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (needs a clock at a year boundary); a unit test can freeze Date to Jan 1 00:30 IST / Dec 31 19:00 UTC and assert the current IST year passes.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test in validators with a mocked clock at the boundary.

findings.title: Houses step's empty-state copy tells members to enter joined/left years 'in the previous step', but the previous step (register) has no year fields — years are only editable in /settings
findings.expected: The instruction points somewhere the fix actually lives.
findings.actual: An alumnus whose yearJoined equals yearLeft (signup allows equality; only left<joined is rejected — actions.ts:77-82) gets `knowsYears=false` and reads 'Tell us the years you joined and left in the previous step, and your years will be laid out here.' Pressing Back shows city/admission/occupation — no year fields (register-step.tsx renders LocationPicker, admissionNumber, jobTitle, workplace only). The member loops between the two steps looking for fields that do not exist; the real editor is /settings, unmentioned.
findings.evidence: houses-step.tsx:50-51: `const knowsYears = user.yearJoined != null && user.yearLeft != null && user.yearLeft - 1 >= user.yearJoined;` and the copy at 88-92 quoted above. Signup guarantees both years non-null for alumni (validators.ts:31-39), so the trigger is exactly the yearLeft === yearJoined case (a one-part-year student), or a teacher... teachers skip this step entirely (onboarding-flow.tsx:92), so it is alumni-only.
findings.fixDirection: Either treat yearLeft === yearJoined as one editable year (the chain editor's real fix), or reword the copy to point at Settings ('add your years in Settings and come back'). Tiny copy+logic change.
findings.reproPlan: Local test signup as alumnus with Joined 2020, Left 2020, Batch 2022; advance to the Houses step and read the copy; press Back.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on the knowsYears predicate + a copy assertion; or fold into an onboarding e2e pass.

findings.title: resetPassword burns the single-use token before writing the new password: a DB failure between the two leaves the member with a spent link and an unchanged password ('That link has already been used')
findings.expected: Token consumption and the password write succeed or fail together (consume inside the same transaction as the update, or consume after the write with a conditional claim).
findings.actual: `readToken(input.token, "reset", { consume: true })` (line 252) marks the row used via updateMany, then ~100-200ms of bcrypt.hash, then a separate `prisma.user.update` (266). A crash, pool timeout, or function freeze between them consumes the link without changing the password; the member's retry reads 'That link has already been used. Ask for a new one if you still need it.' Recovery exists (request another link, 4-per-30-min mint cap), so this is degradation, not loss — but paired with the reset-client's missing try/catch (finding above) the visible symptom is a stuck 'Saving...' button followed by a dead link.
findings.evidence: email-actions.ts:251-263 consume-and-branch, then 265: `const hashed = await bcrypt.hash(input.password, 12); await prisma.user.update({ ... password: hashed, emailVerified: new Date(), credentialVersion: { increment: 1 } })` — two independent write round-trips with CPU work between, no $transaction.
findings.fixDirection: Hash first, then perform the conditional token claim and the user update inside one prisma.$transaction (the claim's `updateMany where usedAt: null` already gives atomic single-winner semantics to reuse inside the tx).
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (requires injecting a failure between two prod DB writes).
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test with a mocked prisma asserting the update and claim share a transaction.

findings.title: If the post-signup auto sign-in fails, onboarding is lost forever: /welcome is only ever reached via the signup client's push, and a manual login lands on /feed with no other entry point to the wizard
findings.expected: A fresh account reaches the setup wizard even when the immediate signIn hiccups (or the tab closes during the 1400ms celebration timer).
findings.actual: On `signInResult?.error` the form shows 'Account created but sign in failed. Please log in manually.' (signup-form.tsx:419); the member logs in at /login and lands on nextPathFromLocation() = /feed. Grep confirms the only navigation to /welcome in the codebase is signup-client.tsx:417's router.push — no login-side redirect for never-onboarded accounts, no nudge on /feed. The wizard (photo, houses, cities — the things that make a profile findable) silently never happens for this cohort. Plausible triggers: the human-pass cookie failing to set (cookie-restricted browsers), an Upstash blip counting the account's budget, closing the tab during the 1400ms window.
findings.evidence: signup-form.tsx:412-419 (signIn then error branch); signup-client.tsx:415-419 (`onSuccess={() => router.push(`/welcome?next=...`)}` — the sole producer); grep for '/welcome' finds only comments elsewhere.
findings.fixDirection: On the manual-login path, detect the never-onboarded state server-side (the same admissionNumber-is-null signal welcome/page.tsx already documents, plus hasSeenOnboarding client-side) and offer /welcome — e.g. login success redirects there when the account is <24h old and admissionNumber is null, or a dismissible 'finish setting up' card on /feed.
findings.reproPlan: Local: sign up, and before the 1400ms timer fires close the tab; reopen the site, log in, observe /feed with no route to the wizard.
findings.gateOrTest: E2e: register, sign out, sign in manually, assert some path to /welcome is offered.

verifiedClean: 6c double-submit server guard on signup: User.email @unique + explicit P2002 catch in registerUser (actions.ts:144-169) returning the friendly already-exists sentence — the constraint-backed guard the taxonomy demands is present; login/signup submit buttons also disable synchronously before the first await

6c server actions re-check auth + Zod: registerUser (trivia pass, Turnstile, signupSchema, consent, rate limit all server-side), saveOnboardingRegister/saveOnboardingHouses/getOnboardingHouses all session-gate and Zod-validate; ID-less by design (they write only the session user's rows)

Turnstile expired-token-on-slow-form-fill: token is fetched only at submit time, handed out exactly once, widget reset after every hand-out and on expired-callback — the slow-form-fill class the brief asked about is handled correctly (only the error-latch case, reported above, is not)
Open-redirect on ?next=: safeNextPath rejects non-'/' starts, '//', backslashes and control chars (next-path.ts:16-25); nextPathFromLocation and the /welcome server page both route through it

CredentialsSignin code plumbing: node_modules/next-auth/react.js does return `code` parsed from the callback URL (verified in the installed beta.32), so rate-limited and bot-check map to their real sentences; unknown/absent codes fall back to the safe generic

React Strict Mode one-shot guards: sessionStorage flags read pure in lazy initializers and consumed in effects (login-client.tsx:52-59,99-110), hasCheckedRef in onboarding-flow.tsx:122-141 — all double-invocation-safe
Landing hero load-in resilience: onLoad + cache-hit check + onError + 6s failsafe all call the idempotent reveal(); loader timers cleaned up on unmount; hero CTAs prefetch /login and /signup

Flight/handoff double-bird protection: fallback reveal timers (6000ms) sit above the flight layer's 5800ms failsafe on both auth pages, reveal is one-shot latched, perch watchers disconnected at handoff

Trivia answer matching boundaries: empty/whitespace-only answers normalize to '' and cannot match (exact match fails, withinOneEdit requires length diff <=1 and 5+ char candidates); 'tree'/'house' bare suffixes deliberately stay wrong

Password-manager whitespace in email fields: all auth email inputs are type=email, whose HTML value-sanitization strips whitespace, and reset-side lowercases/trims server-side; signup rejects malformed with a visible Zod message

Reset flow typed-password preservation: link judged server-side before paint (dead links get their four reasoned screens); a post-load expiry surfaces as an inline error with the typed password still in state; peek-before-consume means a refused weak password never burns the link
Mobile fly-in hydration safety: pre-flight veil is a media-scoped class (max-lg:opacity-0), not an inline style, on all five auth pages — the documented hydration-mismatch class is correctly avoided

onboarding saveOnboardingRegister multi-write: user update + UserPlace deleteMany/createMany wrapped in one $transaction; deliberate non-revalidation of /welcome is argued and correct (revalidating would trip the admissionNumber guard mid-wizard)

Landing page ambient layers at scale (6j): AmbientLeaves/PerchingBirds/LandingNav/FooterHoopoe are all dead behind SHOW_SHOWCASE=false in src/app/page.tsx:127 — nothing animated ships on '/' beyond the hero; the live hero runs no persistent rAF loop (the loader hop loop is bounded and cleaned up)

verify-email token redeemed during render: prefetch/double-click handled via the 'already' outcome and conditional single-winner claim (updateMany where usedAt: null), so racing clicks cannot both win
